doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Checking in with students about how they feel
summary: Stripling and faculty talk about students' mental state, starting lessons with feelings before turning to music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What about the motivation of the students? Did you get a sense of where they’re at?

Yeah. So in talking with other faculty members, we all agreed that it was important to talk to the kids about what they’re feeling too, not just, you can’t ignore that. And one thing about being — and that’s the other reason I never wanted to teach privately like this, because I feel it’s a big responsibility. It wasn’t arrogance on my part, it was me — when I taught at Manhattan School of Music for instance, I just didn’t feel I could give the kind of time because I was going out of town. And so what I did with these lessons is I only taught on Mondays and Tuesdays, and by then I would go out of town for my gigs. What was your original question?
Well I had to do almost the exact same scenario and some of the students seem to work well in the format and others didn’t and I wondered just how do you motivate them?

Right. So good question. What I was saying is, where I was going with that is I felt also I began each lesson with five, ten minutes max if I could, just, how are you feeling? How is this affecting you? Because that’s going to affect how you play, your desire to practice and everything. Some kids were isolated. They hadn’t left — they were scared to leave their room — some kids I had to say maybe you don’t need to go out as often. You know? So everybody was dealing with a mental thing. So I thought it was good to address that for five or ten minutes. And for some it went even longer as to what they were dealing with personally. Then once we got to that, then I got on track with the music. And what I’ve always done with music is let the music be the motivator.
